events.title: Democratisation: closed autocracy to electoral autocracy
events.detail: Derived from a change in the Regimes of the World classification, which is itself built from V-Dem expert ratings. It marks the year a country crossed a threshold, not a specific law or decision.
events.source: derived: Regimes of the World / V-Dem
events.contested: Threshold classifications move in a single step, so the date reflects when a gradual change crossed a line rather than when it began. Read the continuous V-Dem indices alongside this to see the underlying trend.

events.title: Democratic opening: electoral democracy index rose 0.20 over 5 years
events.detail: From 0.06 in 1957 to 0.26 in 1962. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 12%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 337 to 297 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: End of the genocide against the Tutsi
events.detail: The Rwandan Patriotic Front took Kigali, ending roughly a hundred days in which an estimated 800,000 people were killed. A reconstruction programme followed, including the gacaca community courts and later Vision 2020.
events.contested: Post-genocide growth and service delivery are strong by regional standards and widely praised. Human rights organisations document severe restrictions on political competition and press freedom, and some economists question the reliability of the poverty statistics. Aggregate indicators alone cannot settle this.
events.refs: ["UN International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, judgements and findings", "Republic of Rwanda, Vision 2020 (2000)"]
